newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: PRESS DIGEST - S.Korean newspapers - Dec 9.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - S.Korean newspapers - Dec 9.

text.p: The following is a summary of major South Korean political stories in leading newspapers, prepared by Reuters in Seoul. Reuters has not checked the stories and does not gaurantee their accuracy. Telephone: (822) 727-5650. Fax: (822) 727-5666.
- Government, ruling party agree to act on government-initiated labour law revision bill this year.
- A group of 17 North Korean family members and a security guard who reached Hong Kong seeking asylum due to arrive in Seoul today.
- China strengthens policy for North Korea to counter growing influence of United States and Japan, according to a Chinese government source.

- President Kim Young-sam's secretaries have launched a maneuver to drive a wedge between trade union organizations led by hardline leaders, reveals a labour-related document allegedly drafted by the presidential office and obtained by Han-Kyoreh.

- South Korea and the United States are at odds over how to deal with North Korea's threat to suspend sealing used nuclear fuel rods. Washington is pressing Seoul to sign protocol of light-water reactor construction for North Korea, but Seoul is reluctant to comply, demanding Pyongyang's apology for the submarine incursion incident.
- Two alleged North Korean agents in a Hong Kong refugee camp is seeking asylum in South Korea.
- Two North Korean agents are seeking asylum in South Korea, and 17 defectors to arrive in Seoul today.
